title: The Cost of Credit: Interest Rates and Loan Length
seo_title: Grade 8 Cost of Credit and Loans Worksheets (TEKS 8.12A, 8.12B, STAAR)
standard_text: 8.12A solve real-world problems comparing how interest rate and loan length affect the cost of credit; 8.12B calculate the total cost of repaying a loan, including credit cards and easy access loans, under various rates of interest and over different periods using an online calculator
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 personal financial literacy worksheets for Texas TEKS 8.12A and 8.12B: the cost of credit, interest rates, loan length, monthly payments, credit cards and payday loans. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Total cost = principal + interest. Higher rate or longer loan costs more.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • The cost of credit is the interest and fees you pay to borrow money.
  • Simple interest: I = Prt. Total to repay = P + I.
  • A higher interest rate or a longer loan means more interest.
  • Credit card balances and easy-access (payday) loans can cost a lot when they are not paid off quickly.

Examples

Example

$5,000 at 6% for 4 years

I = 5,000 × 0.06 × 4 = 1,200

Answer: total $6,200

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Forgetting to add the principalTotal cost = principal + interest.
Using only one yearMultiply by the number of years in the loan.
Thinking a small fee is a small rateA $45 fee on $300 for 2 weeks is a very high rate.

Calculate the total cost of repaying a loan, including credit cards and easy access loans, under various rates of interest and over different periods using an online calculator.

faq.q: Why does a longer loan cost more?
faq.a: Interest is charged for every year you owe money.

faq.q: Do real loans use simple interest?
faq.a: Many use compound interest; online calculators handle it. Simple interest shows the idea.
